target_customer: Software and AI startups and merchants who receive Stripe and card chargebacks
problem: Merchants lose revenue to chargebacks because writing evidence responses per dispute is manual and templates win less often.
business_model: B2B SaaS, likely performance or subscription based; pricing not found

founders.name: Max Wu
founders.background_notes: YC page gives no prior employers or education.

founders.name: Bowen Xue
founders.background_notes: YC page bio says previously at Together (YC S19); education not stated.

technical_complexity.rationale: Pulling evidence through payment processor APIs and drafting dispute narratives with an LLM is mostly integration plus prompt work; the harder part is tailoring to card network reason codes.

defensibility.rationale: The YC page says responses use past winning disputes, which is a data advantage that grows with volume, but competitors can build similar flows quickly.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not established with dated sources. Stripe offers its own dispute tooling and several automation vendors exist, but none could be tied to a 2023 date in this research.

market_need_then: The YC launch post reports helping 200+ Stripe merchants recover hundreds of thousands of dollars over three months, which is company reported traction after the batch.

identity.voice_and_tone: plain product language; the YC bio says Fighting Stripe disputes

brand_strength.rationale: The ninja fighter metaphor matches the dispute fighting pitch and is memorable, but a search found no press or community about the brand itself.

outcome_analysis: DisputeNinja is an active two person company with no public funding found and no exit. It reports early merchant traction and has Shopify and Stripe oriented distribution, but the market has funded automation vendors and payment processors offering their own tooling. Too little is known to explain a success or failure.
notes: Search hits about a 1.12M seed round belong to a different company (Disputed.ai) and are excluded. A third party profile saying 2025 batch conflicts with the YC S23 listing. No dated competitor sources found for 2023, so the list is empty.
